items.title: Seclusion: The First Break From Coarse Affliction

items.zh: 即此勝解善修、善習、善多修習為因緣故，最初生起斷煩惱道。即所生起斷煩惱道俱行作意，此中說名遠離作意。由能最初斷於欲界先所應斷諸煩惱故，及能除遣彼煩惱品麁重性故。
items.en: Through the causes and conditions of this same confident understanding, well cultivated, well practised, and extensively cultivated, one first gives rise to the path that severs affliction. The mental engagement joined with this arising path that severs affliction is, here, called seclusion. Because it first severs the afflictions that ought first to be severed within the desire realm, and because it dispels the heaviness belonging to that category of affliction.

items.title: Gathering Joy: The First Taste of Freedom's Pleasure

items.zh: 從是已後，愛樂於斷、愛樂遠離，於諸斷中見勝功德，觸證少分遠離喜樂。於時時間，欣樂作意，而深慶悅；於時時間，厭離作意，而深厭患。為欲除遣惛沈睡眠、掉舉等故。
items.en: From this point on, one delights in severing affliction, delights in seclusion, sees excellent merit in each severance, and touches a small measure of the joy and happiness of seclusion. At fitting times, engaging the mind in delight, one deeply rejoices; at fitting times, engaging the mind in revulsion, one deeply feels aversion — in order to dispel dullness, drowsiness, restlessness, and the like.

items.zh: 如是名為攝樂作意。彼由如是樂斷、樂修，正修加行，善品任持，欲界所繫諸煩惱纏若行、若住不復現行。

items.title: Section: Examination — the Tiger the Novice Monk Liked Best

items.zh: 便作是念：我今為有於諸欲中貪欲煩惱不覺知耶？為無有耶？為審觀察如是事故，隨於一種可愛淨相作意思惟。猶未永斷諸隨眠故，思惟如是淨妙相時，便復發起隨習近心、趣習近心、臨習近心、不能住捨，不能厭毀、制伏、違逆。
items.en: One reflects thus: "Do I now have craving towards desires that I am simply unaware of? Or do I not?" In order to carefully examine this very matter, one deliberately directs attention to some attractive, pleasing mark. Because the underlying tendencies have not yet been permanently severed, when reflecting on such an attractive mark, a mind of inclining towards it, of moving towards it, of approaching it arises once again — unable to remain in equanimity, unable to feel revulsion towards it, to master it, or to resist it.

items.zh: 彼作是念：我於諸欲猶未解脫，其心猶未正得解脫，我心仍為諸行制伏，如水被持，未為法性之所制伏。我今復應為欲永斷餘隨眠故，正勤安住樂斷、樂修。如是名為觀察作意。

items.title: Section: The Culmination of Effort and Its Fruit — Entering the First Dhyāna

items.zh: 從此倍更樂斷、樂修，修、奢摩他、毘鉢舍那，鄭重觀察，修習對治，時時觀察先所已斷。由是因緣，從欲界繫一切煩惱，心得離繫。此由暫時伏斷方便，非是畢竟永害種子。當於爾時，初靜慮地前加行道已得究竟，一切煩惱對治作意已得生起。是名加行究竟作意。
items.en: From this point, delighting doubly in severing and in cultivating … through these causes and conditions, the mind becomes freed from every affliction bound to the desire realm. This is only a temporary means of suppression, not the ultimate, permanent destruction of the underlying seeds. At that time, the preparatory path preceding the first dhyāna has reached its culmination, and mental engagement that counters every affliction has fully arisen — this is called the culmination of effort.

items.zh: 從此無間，由是因緣，證入根本初靜慮定。即此根本初靜慮定俱行作意，名加行究竟果作意。
items.en: Immediately following this, without interruption, through these causes and conditions, one enters the root absorption of the first dhyāna itself. The mental engagement joined with this root absorption of the first dhyāna is called the fruit of the culmination of effort.

items.zh: 又於遠離、攝樂作意現在轉時，能適悅身離生喜樂，於時時間，微薄現前。加行究竟作意轉時，即彼喜樂轉復增廣，於時時間，深重現前。加行究竟果作意轉時，離生喜樂遍諸身分，無不充滿，無有間隙。

items.title: Section: The First Dhyāna's Five Factors, and the Seven Engagements' Distinct Functions

items.zh: 彼於爾時，遠離諸欲，遠離一切惡不善法，有尋有伺，離生喜樂，於初靜慮圓滿五支具足安住，名住欲界對治修果，名隨證得離欲界欲。又
items.en: At that time, one is free of desires, free of every unwholesome, unskillful state, endowed with applied and sustained thought, and possessed of the joy and happiness born of seclusion. Abiding with the first dhyāna's five factors fully perfected and complete is called abiding in the fruit of the practice that counters the desire realm, and is called thereby attaining freedom from desire for the desire realm.

items.zh: 了相作意，於所應斷能正了知。於所應得能正了知。為斷應斷，為得應得，心生希願。勝解作意，為斷為得，正發加行。遠離作意，能捨所有上品煩惱。攝樂作意，能捨所有中品煩惱。觀察作意，能於所得離增上慢，安住其心。加行究竟作意，能捨所有下品煩惱。加行究竟果作意，能正領受彼諸作意善修習果。
items.en: Learning the object's mark correctly knows what is to be abandoned and what is to be attained, and, wishing to abandon the one and attain the other, gives rise to genuine aspiration. Confident understanding, for the sake of that abandoning and attaining, actually initiates effort. Seclusion is able to abandon every uppermost grade of affliction. Gathering joy is able to abandon every middle grade of affliction. Examination is able to free what has been attained from false pride, settling the mind securely. The culmination of effort is able to abandon every lowest grade of affliction. The fruit of that culmination correctly receives the fruit that all these mental engagements, well cultivated, have produced.

items.zh: 又若了相作意、若勝解作意，總名隨順作意；厭壞對治俱行。若遠離作意、若加行究竟作意，總名對治作意；斷對治俱行。若攝樂作意，名對治作意及順清淨作意。若觀察作意，名順觀察作意。如是其餘四種作意，當知攝入六作意中。謂隨順作意、對治作意、順清淨作意、順觀察作意。

blocks.text: The remaining attentions, through which the practitioner reaches the first absorption. A short passage (0467a09) is untranslated.
Through well-cultivated confident understanding, "one first gives rise to the path that severs affliction", the coarsest desire-realm afflictions first.

"One delights in severing, delights in seclusion, and touches a small measure of the joy of seclusion." At fitting times one gladdens the mind; at fitting times, feels revulsion; "to dispel dullness and restlessness". Venerable Miào Jìng: those with affliction don't know this joy.

"Do I now have craving towards desires that I am simply unaware of?" To test, "one deliberately directs attention to some attractive mark". If the tendency remains, "a mind of inclining towards it arises once again", and one practises again. Master Cháng Bǎi: for example, one may think one has the first absorption without having it; examination checks.

Delighting in severing and cultivating, the mind is freed from every desire-realm affliction. "This is only temporary suppression, not the permanent destruction of the seeds." Then, "without interruption, one enters the root absorption of the first absorption": the fruit of the culmination.

"Free of desires and unwholesome states, with applied and sustained thought, and the joy and happiness born of seclusion." Each attention has its role: learning the mark knows what to abandon and attain; confident understanding begins the effort; and so on.

quiz.q: "One first gives rise to the path that severs affliction." What counts as such a path, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: once severed, it never reappears in concentration
quiz.why: "Through this confident understanding well cultivated, one first gives rise to the path that severs affliction." Master Cháng Bǎi: once cut off, it never reappears in concentration — that's the path that severs affliction.

quiz.q: Gathering joy "touches a small measure of seclusion's joy." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say of those with affliction?
options: they don't know it — only after cutting affliction do they see how painful it was
quiz.why: "Touches a small measure of the joy and happiness of seclusion." Venerable Miào Jìng: those with affliction don't know it themselves; only after cutting affliction do they realise affliction was painful.

quiz.q: Examination asks, "Do I have craving I'm unaware of?" Why examine, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: e.g., thinking one has the first dhyāna when one hasn't — check by examination
quiz.why: "Do I now have craving towards desires that I am simply unaware of? Or do I not?" Master Cháng Bǎi: for example, not yet having the first dhyāna but thinking one has it — one must check with examination.

quiz.q: "Because tendencies aren't cut, reflecting on attractive marks, inclining arises again." What do the masters say?
options: Miào Jìng: seclusion cut only the heavy desire, the subtle remains; Cháng Bǎi: love cake and cake appears, love beauty and a beauty appears
quiz.why: "Because the underlying tendencies have not yet been permanently severed, when reflecting on such an attractive mark, a mind of inclining towards it arises once again." Venerable Miào Jìng: seclusion only cut the heavy desire; the subtle remains. Master Cháng Bǎi: if one loves cake, a cake appears; if one likes beautiful women, a beauty appears.

quiz.q: The mind is freed from desire-realm affliction, "only temporary suppression, not destroying seeds." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: only temporary suppression — mundane absorption, not the noble path, not cutting seeds
quiz.why: "This is only a temporary means of suppression, not the ultimate, permanent destruction of the underlying seeds." Master Cháng Bǎi: this only temporarily suppresses — a means of cutting desire through mundane absorption; without the noble path, desire's seeds aren't ultimately cut.

quiz.q: "Immediately following, one enters the root first dhyāna." How does Master Cháng Bǎi relate the culmination and its fruit?
options: the culmination suppresses all three grades; the next instant is the fruit — the first dhyāna
quiz.why: "Immediately following this, without interruption, through these causes and conditions, one enters the root absorption of the first dhyāna itself." Master Cháng Bǎi: the culmination suppresses upper, middle, and lower grades of affliction; the next instant attests the fruit of that culmination — the first dhyāna attained.

quiz.q: Learning the mark "gives rise to aspiration"; confident understanding "initiates effort." How does Venerable Miào Jìng sum it up?
options: the first is vow, confident understanding is practice — vow and practice
quiz.why: "Confident understanding, for the sake of that abandoning and attaining, actually initiates effort." Venerable Miào Jìng: the former is "vow," confident understanding is "practice" — that's the sense of vow and practice. Master Cháng Bǎi likewise says every practice needs faith, vow, and practice.
